title: Singhs who Accepted Martyrdom {(Satguru) picked up a sword}

blocks.text: Dohra:

If someone raises a question (about martyrdom), How the title martyr came to be associated (with the Singhs)? Was this title attached to the Singhs by Guru Gobind Singh, Or was this association made earlier by somebody else? (1)
lines: If someone raises a question (about martyrdom),
How the title martyr came to be associated (with the Singhs)?
Was this title attached to the Singhs by Guru Gobind Singh,
Or was this association made earlier by somebody else?

blocks.text: Chaupai:

This question should be answered in the way, As author is going to narrate after hearing (from his elders). The way the author has beard the episode from his ancestors, He has narrated it to the best of his knowledge. (2)
lines: This question should be answered in the way,
As author is going to narrate after hearing (from his elders).
The way the author has beard the episode from his ancestors,
He has narrated it to the best of his knowledge.

blocks.text: Dohra:

One day Satguru, Guru Gobind Singh was sitting (at Anandpur Sahib), Seated on his ceremonial seat at Damdama holding a congregation. A Sikh arrived there while reciting Gurbani hymns, And presented himself before Guru Gobind Singh. (3)
lines: One day Satguru,
Guru Gobind Singh was sitting (at Anandpur Sahib),
Seated on his ceremonial seat at Damdama holding a congregation.
A Sikh arrived there while reciting Gurbani hymns,
And presented himself before Guru Gobind Singh.

blocks.text: Ardil:

He remarked that sons of the Sikhs had lost faith in the Guru, And that in the age of Kaliyuga Sikhs with faith had turned faithless. Hearing this the Guru remarked that the wavering ones alone had turned faithless, The faithfuls were still intact and flourishing well in their faith. (4)
lines: He remarked that sons of the Sikhs had lost faith in the Guru,
And that in the age of Kaliyuga Sikhs with faith had turned faithless.
Hearing this the Guru remarked that the wavering ones alone had turned faithless,
The faithfuls were still intact and flourishing well in their faith.

blocks.text: The Sikh asked if there were any faithful Sikhs present in the congregation, Who kept their faith in the darkage of Kaliyuga as they did in Satyuga. That such faithful Sikhs, if any, be presented before the congregation. So that their one glimpse would all his sins like a dip in a holy place. (5)
lines: The Sikh asked if there were any faithful Sikhs present in the congregation,
Who kept their faith in the darkage of Kaliyuga as they did in Satyuga.
That such faithful Sikhs, if any, be presented before the congregation.
So that their one glimpse would all his sins like a dip in a holy place.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The Guru enacted a drama for defining the Sikhs, In order to distinguish between the faithful and the faithless. Sri Satguru Gobind Singh remarked from his sacred lips, That he wished to put his Sikhs to a test. (6)
lines: The Guru enacted a drama for defining the Sikhs,
In order to distinguish between the faithful and the faithless.
Sri Satguru Gobind Singh remarked from his sacred lips,
That he wished to put his Sikhs to a test.

blocks.text: Then His Holiness, calling for a double-edged dagger to be brought, Ordered the tribal black smiths to sharpen both of its edges. Then brandishing this double edged weapon with his arm, The Guru declared his wish to behead five of his Sikhs. (7)
lines: Then His Holiness, calling for a double-edged dagger to be brought,
Ordered the tribal black smiths to sharpen both of its edges.
Then brandishing this double edged weapon with his arm,
The Guru declared his wish to behead five of his Sikhs.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Then, in the midst of congregation which assembled there, The Guru made an open declaration addressed to everyone. Was there any (faithful) Sikh present in the congregation, Who was willing (voluntarily) to be beheaded? (8)
lines: Then, in the midst of congregation which assembled there,
The Guru made an open declaration addressed to everyone.
Was there any (faithful) Sikh present in the congregation,
Who was willing (voluntarily) to be beheaded?

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Hearing these words, people felt scared (of the Guru), While many of them ran away from the congregation. Some of them remarked that the Guru was a hardened obstinate, Who wished to dismantle and destroy the Sikh religion. (9)
lines: Hearing these words, people felt scared (of the Guru),
While many of them ran away from the congregation.
Some of them remarked that the Guru was a hardened obstinate,
Who wished to dismantle and destroy the Sikh religion.

blocks.text: While some ran towards their homes after hearing the Guru, Others, on their way, were asked to return home midway. Some met the Guru, some returned after meeting the Guru, But none of them looked back while fleeing from there. (10)
lines: While some ran towards their homes after hearing the Guru,
Others, on their way, were asked to return home midway.
Some met the Guru, some returned after meeting the Guru,
But none of them looked back while fleeing from there.

blocks.text: Some remarked that the Guru had killed the sons of Masands, And that he had been cruel from the beginning. Finally, only Majhail Singhs, remained to be tested, Who had the blessings of the sacred shrine at Amritsar. (11)
lines: Some remarked that the Guru had killed the sons of Masands,
And that he had been cruel from the beginning.
Finally, only Majhail Singhs, remained to be tested,
Who had the blessings of the sacred shrine at Amritsar.

blocks.text: Bhai Gurdas1 had remarked about such faithful Sikhs, That the Guru enacted dramatic situations to test his Sikhs' faith. And that those Sikhs who had full faith in the Guru, Obeyed the Guru's command that the Guru dictated. (12)
lines: Bhai Gurdas1 had remarked about such faithful Sikhs,
That the Guru enacted dramatic situations to test his Sikhs' faith.
And that those Sikhs who had full faith in the Guru,
Obeyed the Guru's command that the Guru dictated.

blocks.text: Dohra:

From the moment, the Guru had founded the sacred pool, In the Majha region of Punjab in the country, Anyone who had a dip in this sacred pool (at Amritsar), Got rid of all his sins (with the grace of the Guru). (13)
lines: From the moment, the Guru had founded the sacred pool,
In the Majha region of Punjab in the country,
Anyone who had a dip in this sacred pool (at Amritsar),
Got rid of all his sins (with the grace of the Guru).

blocks.text: Sorath Mahalla 5 (Sri Guru Granth Sahib) The fifth Sikh Guru, Sri Arjan Dev ji writes : "With the intercession of the creator (God), Not a least harm has come to me.
A dip in the sacred pool has proved efficacious, And meditation on God's name has eliminated all my sins. (1)
lines: A dip in the sacred pool has proved efficacious,
And meditation on God's name has eliminated all my sins.

blocks.text: Revered saints, the sacred pool founded by Guru Ramdas is auspicious, Whosoever takes a holy dip here redeems his whole generation, As well as achieves redemption for his own soul (1)
lines: Revered saints, the sacred pool founded by Guru Ramdas is auspicious,
Whosoever takes a holy dip here redeems his whole generation,
As well as achieves redemption for his own soul

blocks.text: pause. Such a person gets name and fame in the world, As well as gets all his cherished desires fulfilled. A holy dip protects and saves one's soul, And makes one meditate on god's sacred name. (2)
lines: pause.
Such a person gets name and fame in the world,
As well as gets all his cherished desires fulfilled.
A holy dip protects and saves one's soul,
And makes one meditate on god's sacred name.

blocks.text: Whosoever takes a dip in the sacred pool, He achieves eternal salvation for his soul. He gets liberated from the cycle of birth and death, By meditating upon the sacred name of God. (3)
lines: Whosoever takes a dip in the sacred pool,
He achieves eternal salvation for his soul.
He gets liberated from the cycle of birth and death,
By meditating upon the sacred name of God.

blocks.text: He alone gets a revelation about the creator, Who becomes worthy of His Divine grace. Nanak has sought protection of the Divine God, Which has relieved him of all his worries and tensions." (4)
lines: He alone gets a revelation about the creator,
Who becomes worthy of His Divine grace.
Nanak has sought protection of the Divine God,
Which has relieved him of all his worries and tensions."

blocks.text: Chaupai:

With Guru's grace, they (the Majhail Singhs) imbibed their faith, Which effaced all traces of cowardice from their system. A dip in the holy pool removes all traces of taint from heart and body, And a cleansed heart and mind is enriched with wisdom. (14)
lines: With Guru's grace, they (the Majhail Singhs) imbibed their faith,
Which effaced all traces of cowardice from their system.
A dip in the holy pool removes all traces of taint from heart and body,
And a cleansed heart and mind is enriched with wisdom.

blocks.text: As these Majhail Singhs heard the Guru's command, They felt as excited as a devout Sikh feels (at Guru's words). Each one competed with the other to stand ahead of his rival, As there were so many who wished to be beheaded by the Guru. (15)
lines: As these Majhail Singhs heard the Guru's command,
They felt as excited as a devout Sikh feels (at Guru's words).
Each one competed with the other to stand ahead of his rival,
As there were so many who wished to be beheaded by the Guru.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Satguru had ordered for a big tent to be pitched. And get it covered with a curtain from all sides. Goats were also kept inside the tent secretly, Without anybody being informed of this plan. (16)
lines: Satguru had ordered for a big tent to be pitched.
And get it covered with a curtain from all sides.
Goats were also kept inside the tent secretly,
Without anybody being informed of this plan.

blocks.text: When the Guru made a demand for human heads, The Majhail Singhs came forward to offer their heads. After washing their bodies and sprinkling themselves with perfumes, Very handsome, muscular youth volunteered themselves for sacrifice. (17)
lines: When the Guru made a demand for human heads,
The Majhail Singhs came forward to offer their heads.
After washing their bodies and sprinkling themselves with perfumes,
Very handsome, muscular youth volunteered themselves for sacrifice.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Satguru, selecting five Singhs out of these volunteers, Enacted this drama making them the dramatis personae, Making them stand after blindfolding all of them, The Guru slaughtered the goats in their presence. (18)
lines: Satguru, selecting five Singhs out of these volunteers,
Enacted this drama making them the dramatis personae,
Making them stand after blindfolding all of them,
The Guru slaughtered the goats in their presence.

blocks.text: As the blood stream from the goats' slaughter gushed forth, The people ran out scared for their lives. The Guru, after saving the lives of his devout Sikhs, Honoured them with the honour of being martyrs. (19)
lines: As the blood stream from the goats' slaughter gushed forth,
The people ran out scared for their lives.
The Guru, after saving the lives of his devout Sikhs,
Honoured them with the honour of being martyrs.
